instructions: Stand on one foot on a stair or on flat floor, holding a wall or rail for balance.
Lower your heel as far as is comfortable.
Rise as high onto the ball of the foot as you can.
Pause at the top, lower slowly and switch legs after the set.
cues: Use a stair edge for a bigger stretch.
Two seconds up, two seconds down.

name: Bent-knee calf raise
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and bend your knees slightly, holding a wall for balance.
Keep the knee bend fixed.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Lower slowly and repeat.
cues: The bent knee shifts work to the lower calf.
Keep weight over the big toe.
commonMistakes: Straightening the knees as you rise.
Rolling onto the outside of the feet.

name: Standing dumbbell calf raise
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet hip-width apart.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause for a second at the top.
Lower your heels slowly to the floor.
cues: Hold one dumbbell and do one leg at a time for more load.

name: Seated dumbbell calf raise
instructions: Sit on the end of a bench with feet flat and a dumbbell resting on each knee.
Put the balls of your feet on a book or step if you have one.
Lift your heels as high as you can.
Lower slowly and repeat.
cues: Hold the top for a second.
Keep the dumbbells steady on your knees.
commonMistakes: Lifting the dumbbells with your hands.

name: Bodyweight triceps extension
instructions: Place your hands on a sturdy kitchen counter or table edge and walk your feet back into a leaning plank.
Bend only at the elbows to lower your forehead toward your hands.
Keep the elbows pointing down, not flaring.
Straighten your arms to push back to the start.
cues: A higher surface makes it easier.
Keep the body in one straight line.
commonMistakes: Turning it into a push-up by moving at the shoulders.

name: Kneeling pike push-up
instructions: Kneel on a mat, place your hands under your shoulders and lift your hips so your body makes an upside-down V from knees to hands.
Walk your knees in until your hips are high over your shoulders.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor in front of your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
cues: Head travels forward of the hands, making a triangle.
commonMistakes: Letting it turn into a flat push-up.

name: Wall handstand hold
instructions: Place your hands a hand-width from a wall, shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet up the wall while walking your hands closer until your chest faces the wall.
Push the floor away and hold a straight line from hands to heels.
Walk down slowly; build up to 20 to 40 second holds.
commonMistakes: Holding past the point where form breaks.

name: Prone lat pulldown
instructions: Lie face down with your arms reaching straight overhead and lift your hands and chest a little off the floor.
Pull your elbows down and back toward your ribs as if doing a pulldown, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Hold for two seconds with the chest still lifted.
Reach back overhead without touching down and repeat.
cues: Think of bending the bar you are pulling.
Keep the neck long and eyes on the floor.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chest too high and straining the lower back.

name: Floor triceps dip
instructions: Sit on the floor with knees bent and hands behind your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet.
Lift your hips a little off the floor.
Bend your elbows to lower your upper body toward the floor, then straighten them to push back up.
Keep the hips lifted for the whole set.
cues: Elbows point straight back, not out.
Move your feet further away to make it harder.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop to the floor between reps.

name: Reverse Nordic
instructions: Kneel upright on a mat with knees hip-width apart and toes tucked or flat.
Keep a straight line from knees to head and lean back slowly.
Go only as far as you can control, then pull yourself back up with your thighs.
Start with a small range and build depth over weeks.
cues: Squeeze your glutes to keep the hips straight.
commonMistakes: Bending at the hips to make it easier.
Dropping into a range you cannot return from.

name: Glute bridge walkout
instructions: Lie on your back and lift into a glute bridge with feet under your knees.
Keeping the hips up, take small heel steps away from you until your legs are nearly straight.
Walk the heels back in to the start.
Lower the hips only at the end of the set.
cues: Hips stay high the whole time.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag as the feet move out.
Arching the lower back instead of using the hamstrings.
